items.title: Brand value can exceed half of market capitalisation
items.claim: Interbrand's 2023 Best Global Brands ranking valued Apple's brand at around $502 billion. What's the relationship between brand value and accounting?

options.text: Brand value appears directly on the balance sheet for all firms
Under IFRS / UK GAAP, internally generated brands are not recognised as balance sheet assets; purchased brands can be. Apple's $502bn estimate is an external valuation, not a reported figure
Brand value equals market cap minus debt
Brand value has no relationship with share price

items.reveal:
IAS 38 prohibits capitalising internally generated brands; accounting wants to avoid the manipulability of self-assessed intangibles. Acquired brands (e.g. Cadbury bought by Kraft for £11.5bn in 2010) appear at acquisition cost as 'goodwill' or identified intangibles.

Interbrand, Kantar BrandZ and Brand Finance use different methodologies — discounted cash flow from brand-attributable earnings — and produce different rankings. The numbers are estimates, but the underlying point is real: a meaningful share of S&P 500 market value sits in intangibles invisible on balance sheets.
items.why: Investors price intangibles even when accountants don't book them. The gap between book and market value for brand-heavy firms is largely brand and goodwill.

items.title: Maximising capacity utilisation isn't always optimal
items.claim: A factory runs at 95% capacity utilisation. Which statement is most accurate?

options.text: This is always the optimal level
Running close to maximum capacity leaves no slack for demand surges, breakdowns or staff absence and tends to raise unit costs through overtime and quality problems
Capacity utilisation has no link to unit cost
Unit costs fall continuously with utilisation

items.reveal:
Hospitals running at >90% bed occupancy have measurably worse patient outcomes (NHS England analyses through the 2010s). Airlines running above 85% load factor face cascading delay risk. Manufacturing plants above 90% have higher defect rates and overtime costs.

Operations researchers use Kingman's formula: waiting time grows non-linearly as utilisation approaches 100%. The textbook assumption that high utilisation is good ignores queueing dynamics.
items.why: Headline utilisation numbers hide trade-offs. The optimal level depends on demand variability, not just on fixed-cost recovery.

items.title: ROCE compares like with like across firm sizes
items.claim: A firm has operating profit of £2 million, total assets of £15 million and current liabilities of £5 million. What is ROCE?
items.reveal_title: Operating profit divided by capital employed
items.reveal:
Capital employed = total assets - current liabilities = £15m - £5m = £10m. ROCE = £2m / £10m = 20%.

ROCE is the most commonly cited single profitability measure in UK A-level. It is benchmarked against the cost of capital — if a firm consistently earns less than its weighted cost of capital, it is destroying shareholder value. UK FTSE 100 firms have averaged 10-15% ROCE over the last decade.
items.why: Absolute profit figures don't tell you whether capital was well used. A £2m profit from £10m of capital is 20%; the same profit from £100m of capital is 2%.
